claims.text: The investigated alloy is equimolar WTaTiVZr.
WTaTiVZr has enhanced plastic strain and toughness relative to pure tungsten at high temperature.
The enhanced plastic strain and toughness arise from dynamic phase-transformation strengthening.
Severe lattice distortion and multielement interactions in WTaTiVZr promote transient nanoscale chemically short-range-ordered clusters near dislocation cores during loading.
The short-range-ordered clusters impede and regulate dislocation motion.
Cluster-mediated regulation of dislocations delays dislocation localization, crack nucleation, and crack initiation.
Delaying dislocation localization and crack nucleation increases plastic-strain capacity and toughness.
The initial equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy is likely a single-phase BCC solid solution with significant lattice distortion.
Pure tungsten has a more uniform lattice and lacks the proposed dynamic nanocluster-formation mechanism.
Elevated-temperature nanoindentation creep testing has been performed on the same TaTiVWZr alloy system and compared with pure tungsten.
Identically loading WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten by creep and in situ tensile tests would provide a controlled comparison.
Temperatures of approximately 800–1200 °C are representative of sustained plasma-facing-component service for this comparison.
Relative to pure tungsten, WTaTiVZr will exhibit a lower creep rate.
Relative to pure tungsten, WTaTiVZr will exhibit more stable and homogeneous dislocation structures and higher fracture toughness and ductility.
The appearance of nanoclusters at dislocation sites will correlate with improved creep, ductility, and toughness.
The proposed mechanism may cease to operate at lower temperatures because dynamic transformation and short-range ordering are less activated.
Phase-transformation strengthening has previously been identified as a high-temperature strengthening mechanism in alloys related to turbine-disk applications.

In another high- or medium-entropy alloy context, hierarchical twinning and intersecting twin boundaries can hinder dislocations, produce strain hardening, and promote homogeneous plastic deformation and toughness.
Failure to observe dynamic nanocluster formation near dislocations, or failure to observe significantly improved mechanical properties relative to tungsten, would falsify the hypothesis.
